definition: Additional computation applied at inference time (rather than during training) to improve a model's output quality, such as generating and evaluating multiple reasoning paths.
details: Increasing test-time compute — for example, through extended chain-of-thought reasoning or self-verification — has emerged as an important lever for improving model performance on hard problems, complementing gains from scaling training compute.

explainer.lead: Test-time compute is additional computation applied at inference rather than during training to improve output quality. It matters as a lever for hard problems that complements gains from scaling training compute.

tiers.eli5: You can let the model think longer before answering, like giving someone extra time to work through a difficult problem.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers spend more inference compute, for example through extended chain-of-thought reasoning or self-verification, to raise performance on hard problems. The facts here do not detail cost trade-offs.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as extra inference-time computation, such as generating and evaluating multiple reasoning paths; it complements training-compute scaling. No formal formula is given here.

explainer.example: A model generates several reasoning paths and evaluates them, using longer chain-of-thought to improve its answer on a difficult problem.
